reader_sentence: The figure shows that linear probes can decode more abstract concepts only from deeper layers: part of speech becomes decodable at layer 1, sentiment at layer 5, named entity type at layer 10, and statement truthfulness at layer 17, with each rising from chance (50%) to about 90–95% held-out accuracy.
intended: The four concepts become decodable at clearly different depths: part of speech first (around layer 3), then sentiment (around layer 8), named entity type (around layer 13 to 14), and statement truthfulness last (around layer 19).
reason: The reader gets the key finding right: the four concepts become decodable at distinct, increasing depths in the same order. Their layer numbers run consistently 2–4 layers earlier than intended, probably because they marked where accuracy starts rising rather than its midpoint.
